title: Bioflux Analyses: Image Preprocessing
author: Tobias Weise
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bb7uirnw

steps.title: Extract frames from video
steps.instruction: Convert the source .AVI video into single grayscale .TIFF images and create a metadata DataFrame using OpenCV‑Python.

substeps.instruction: Import required packages: `import numpy as np`, `import pandas as pd`, `import cv2`.
Open the video: `cap = cv2.VideoCapture(source_path + '/video_file.AVI')`.
Initialize frame counter `i = 0`.
While the video is opened, read each frame (`ret, frame = cap.read()`).
If `ret` is False, break the loop.
Convert the frame to grayscale: `frame = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)`.
Save the frame as a .TIFF file: `cv2.imwrite(target_path + 'frame_%s.TIFF' % i, frame)`.
Increment `i` and repeat until all frames are processed.
Release the video capture and close windows (`cap.release(); cv2.destroyAllWindows()`).
Create and store a metadata DataFrame (e.g., `pd.DataFrame()` saved with `to_pickle`).

steps.title: Estimate rotation angles
steps.instruction: For each image, determine the rotation angle that minimizes the X‑direction peak width of chamber edges using a basin‑hopping optimizer (200 iterations, initial angle 0°).

substeps.instruction: Import required packages: `import numpy as np`, `import pandas as pd`, `import cv2`, `import skimage`, `import scipy`.
Define a scoring function `score(a)` that:
‑ Rotates the image by angle `a` with `skimage.transform.rotate(img, a, resize=True)`.
‑ Computes the median pixel intensity for each row (y‑axis).
‑ Creates a DataFrame of these medians, calculates the absolute first‑order difference, and selects rows where the difference is ≥ the 98th percentile.
‑ Clusters the selected rows into four equal‑size groups and computes the width of each cluster.
‑ Returns the sum of the four cluster widths (the score to minimise).
Load the existing metadata DataFrame: `data = pd.read_pickle(data_path + 'data.pkl')`.
Create an empty array for angles: `angle = np.zeros(len(data))`.
Loop over each image index `i`:
‑ Read and invert the image: `img = 255 - skimage.io.imread(source_path + 'frame_%s.TIF' % i)`.
‑ Run basin‑hopping: `answ = scipy.optimize.basinhopping(score, 0, niter=200)`.
‑ Store the optimal angle: `angle[i] = answ.x[0]`.
Add the angle array to the metadata (`data['angle'] = angle`) and save the DataFrame back to disk.

steps.title: Determine chamber edge lines
steps.instruction: Identify six chamber edge positions per rotated image by median‑intensity profiling, 98th‑percentile thresholding, four‑cluster assignment, and a 5‑pixel safety offset.

substeps.instruction: Import required packages: `import numpy as np`, `import pandas as pd`, `import skimage`.
Define function `find_lines(img)` that:
‑ Inverts the image (`img_bin = 255 - img`).
‑ Computes row‑wise median intensity (`xmedian`).
‑ Creates a DataFrame, calculates absolute differences (`xdiff`), and selects rows with `xdiff` ≥ the 98th percentile.
‑ Resets the index and assigns each row to one of four clusters (`pd.cut`).
‑ For each cluster, finds the maximum (or minimum) `imgdex` value, adds or subtracts 5 pixels, and stores the result in a six‑element array `imgdex`.
‑ Returns `imgdex` as an integer NumPy array.
Load the metadata DataFrame (`data = pd.read_pickle(data_path + 'data.pkl')`).
Initialize six zero arrays for line positions (`line1` … `line6`).
Loop over each image index `i`:
‑ Read the image (`img = skimage.io.imread(source_path + 'frame_%s.TIFF' % i)`).
‑ Rotate the image using the median angle from metadata (`img = skimage.transform.rotate(img, data.angle.median(), resize=True, mode='constant', cval=1)`).
‑ Call `find_lines(img)` to obtain the six line positions.
‑ Store each position in the corresponding line array.
Convert all line arrays to integer dtype with `pd.to_numeric(..., downcast='integer')`.
Add the six line columns to the metadata DataFrame and save it (`data.to_pickle(data_path + 'data.pkl')`).

steps.title: Cut images into chambers
steps.instruction: Using the stored line positions, slice each rotated image into wild‑type and mutant chambers with a 10‑pixel horizontal safety margin and save as unsigned‑integer TIFF files.

substeps.instruction: Import required packages: `import numpy as np`, `import pandas as pd`, `import skimage`, `from skimage import img_as_uint`, `import cv2`.
Load the metadata DataFrame (`data = pd.read_pickle(data_path + 'data.pkl')`).
Loop over each image index `i`:
‑ Print progress (`print('processing file ', i+1, ' of ', len(data))`).
‑ Read the image (`img = skimage.io.imread(source_path + 'frame_%s.TIFF' % i)`).
‑ Rotate the image with the median angle (`img = skimage.transform.rotate(img, data.angle.median(), resize=False)`).
‑ Slice the wild‑type chamber:
`img_cham_A = img[data.line1[i]:data.line2[i], 10:len(img[0]) - 10]`.
‑ Slice the mutant chamber:
`img_cham_B = img[data.line5[i]:data.line6[i], 10:len(img[0]) - 10]`.
‑ Save the chambers as unsigned‑integer TIFFs:
`skimage.io.imsave(target_path + '00_WT/frame_%s_WT.TIFF' % i, img_as_uint(img_cham_A))`
`skimage.io.imsave(target_path + '01_MT/frame_%s_MT.TIFF' % i, img_as_uint(img_cham_B))`.

steps.title: Calculate mean intensity and growth rate
steps.instruction: Compute mean gray intensity for each chamber at every time point, add to the metadata, create a time column (measurements every 20 min → index/3 h), and derive growth rates µ using the central‑difference formula.

substeps.instruction: Import required packages: `import numpy as np`, `import pandas as pd`, `import skimage`, `from skimage import img_as_float`.
Load the metadata DataFrame (`data = pd.read_pickle(data_path + 'data.pkl')`).
Create a time column in hours: `data['time'] = data.index / 3` (since each index corresponds to a 20 min interval).
Allocate zero arrays for mean and variance values:
‑ `meanGrayWT, meanGrayMT, varGrayWT, varGrayMT = [np.zeros(len(data)) for _ in range(4)]`.
Loop over each frame index `k`:
‑ Read the wild‑type image, convert to float, invert:
`imgWT = 1 - img_as_float(skimage.io.imread(source_path + '00_WT/frame_%s_WT.TIF' % k))`.
‑ Read the mutant image similarly:
`imgMT = 1 - img_as_float(skimage.io.imread(source_path + '01_MT/frame_%s_MT.TIF' % k))`.
‑ Calculate mean gray values:
`meanGrayWT[k] = np.mean(imgWT)`
`meanGrayMT[k] = np.mean(imgMT)`.
Add the mean columns to the DataFrame (`data['greyWTint'] = meanGrayWT`, `data['greyMTint'] = meanGrayMT`).
Compute growth rates using the central difference approximation:
‑ `data['greyWTmu'] = np.gradient(data.greyWTint) / data.greyWTint * 3`
‑ `data['greyMTmu'] = np.gradient(data.greyMTint) / data.greyMTint * 3`
Save the updated DataFrame (`data.to_pickle(data_path + 'data.pkl')`).

steps.title: Visualise results (optional)
steps.instruction: Plot mean pixel intensities and calculated growth rates for wild‑type (black) and mutant (red/blue) strains as shown in Figure 3.1.

description: Chamber Selection and Background Removal Chambers were selected from the respective video frame between the determined chamber edges (according to Fig. 2.1-D). In order to exclude the chamber edge itself, a safety distance of 5 pixels in X-direction is applied. Also, a background removal was performed by subtracting the median intensity of the reference space resolved in Y-direction. Reference was selected as a 100 pixel wide strip next to cluster 1 (Fig. 2.1-D). Example code of background removal execution. # load meta data frame from file data = pd.read_pickle((data_path + 'data.pkl')) # loop over all images for i in range(len(data)): clear_output() print('sample',k+1,'processing file ',i+1,' of ',len(data)) # read respective image # read + rotate original image img = cv2.imread((source_path + 'frame_%s.TIFF'%i),0) img = skimage.transform.rotate(img,data.angle.median(),resize=False) img = img_as_ubyte(img) # invert image img = 255 - img # read chamber images img_cham_A = cv2.imread((source_path + '00_WT/frame_%s_WT.TIFF'%i),0) img_cham_B = cv2.imread((source_path + '01_MT/frame_%s_MT.TIFF'%i),0) # invert chamber images img_cham_A = 255 - img_cham_A img_cham_B = 255 - img_cham_B # rotate chamber images 90° img_cham_A = np.array([list(i) for i in zip(*img_cham_A)], dtype=np.int16) img_cham_B = np.array([list(i) for i in zip(*img_cham_B)], dtype=np.int16) # cut reference space (+ invert) refspace = img[data.line3[i]:data.line3[i]+100, 10:len(img[0])-10] # rotate refspace 90° refspace90 = np.array([list(i) for i in zip(*refspace)], dtype=np.int16) # calculate median intensity of background background = np.zeros(len(refspace90)) for j in range(len(refspace90)): background[j] = np.median(refspace90[j]) background = np.array(background,dtype=np.int16) # create new empty image cham_A_new = np.zeros(img_cham_A.shape, dtype=np.int16) cham_B_new = np.zeros(img_cham_B.shape, dtype=np.int16) # subtract background for l in
